title: Problems & Complaints
description: Complaining politely and getting things sorted at a café, a shop or a homestay. A calm maaf and a soft request get further than a raised voice.

phrases.english: Sorry, this isn't what I ordered.
phrases.registerNotes: Starting with maaf keeps it polite even when the mistake is theirs.
phrases.pitfallNote: Bukan, not tidak: you're saying it isn't a thing (pesanan, your order).

phrases.indonesian: Maaf, tadi saya pesan yang tidak pedas.
phrases.english: Sorry, I asked for it not spicy.
phrases.registerNotes: Tadi, 'earlier', points back to when you ordered; yang tidak pedas is 'the not-spicy one'.

phrases.indonesian: Maaf, sepertinya ada yang salah. Bisa tolong dicek lagi?
phrases.english: Sorry, I think there's a mistake. Could you check it again?
phrases.registerNotes: Sepertinya, 'it seems', leaves room for the mistake to be yours. Use it for a bill, a booking or a delivery.
phrases.cultureNote: Saving face matters: a complaint that lets the other person put things right without blame gets results faster.

phrases.registerNotes: Rusak follows the thing that’s broken: AC-nya rusak, kuncinya rusak. Say it at reception, then ask Bisa diperbaiki?
phrases.pitfallNote: Rusak is broken or not working (a lock, a zip, a TV); things that won't switch on are mati: Lampunya mati.

phrases.registerNotes: The di- form asks for it to be fixed without saying who should do it, which sounds softer. You'll also hear dibetulkan, or casually dibenerin.

phrases.english: Can I exchange it for a new one?
phrases.registerNotes: Tukar is to swap or exchange. Bring the receipt (struk) and the packaging.

phrases.english: Can I get my money back?
phrases.registerNotes: Literally 'can the money be returned?'. In apps and online shops people simply say refund.
phrases.cultureNote: Receipts often say Barang yang sudah dibeli tidak dapat ditukar atau dikembalikan (no exchanges or returns), so check before you pay.

phrases.indonesian: Kamarnya berisik sekali. Bisa pindah kamar?
phrases.english: The room is really noisy. Could I change rooms?
phrases.registerNotes: Say what the noise is if you can: suara jalan (traffic noise), suara musik.
phrases.pitfallNote: Berisik is noisy and annoying; ramai is busy or lively, often a good thing.

phrases.indonesian: Air di kamar mandi tidak keluar.
phrases.english: The water's not running in the bathroom.
phrases.registerNotes: Literally 'the water doesn't come out'. You'll also hear Airnya mati (the water's off).
phrases.cultureNote: Homes with a water pump (pompa air) lose water when the power goes off, so check that too.

phrases.indonesian: Maaf, saya sudah menunggu dari tadi.
phrases.english: Excuse me, I've been waiting for quite a while.
phrases.registerNotes: Dari tadi, 'since earlier', makes the point without sounding angry. For food that hasn't come: Pesanan saya belum datang, ya?
phrases.cultureNote: Showing anger embarrasses everyone and rarely speeds things up; a calm, smiling complaint is taken more seriously.

phrases.english: Sorry, I've been given the wrong change.
phrases.registerNotes: Kurang, 'less', says something's missing; add how much: Kembaliannya kurang dua ribu (It's two thousand short).

phrases.english: Could I speak to the manager?
phrases.registerNotes: Keep it for when a calm word with the staff hasn't worked. In a small place, ask for the owner: pemiliknya.
phrases.cultureNote: Asking for the manager in front of others shames the staff member, so say it quietly.

phrases.indonesian: Tidak apa-apa. Terima kasih atas bantuannya.
phrases.english: No worries. Thanks for your help.
phrases.registerNotes: Ending on thanks once it's sorted leaves everyone on good terms. Among friends, Nggak apa-apa, makasih, ya.
